props.text: All file uploads pass through the API gateway
The API gateway enforces a 10 MB request body limit
Our Elasticsearch mapping cannot take incremental updates
The SOC 2 auditor requires credential rotation at most every 90 days
A rollback requires a manual database restore
The engineering team is under 15 people
All EU customers are in Germany and Austria
Notification volume is under 100 emails a day, inside the SendGrid free tier
CI runs no automated test suite
The web tier must stay stateless so it can autoscale
RDS does not support customer-managed encryption keys in eu-central-1
Multi-currency billing is not enabled on our Stripe account
Safari versions below 15 are under 1% of traffic
GDPR applies to our EU users
LaunchDarkly costs under $500 a month at our seat count
There is no end-to-end test coverage of the web app
Warehouse query cost scales with how often the pipeline runs
We are on BigQuery on-demand pricing
The payments SDK does not support the React Native New Architecture
We plan to shard Postgres by tenant
Only four engineers are trained for on-call
Free-tier bots are abusing public sign-up
Log storage costs about $0.50 per GB a month
SOC 2 requires infrastructure to be reproducible from code
Chrome will remove third-party cookies in 2025
We need SOC 2 certification to sell to enterprise customers
Tooling and infrastructure spend must stay under $20,000 a month
We sell to customers in the European Union

Google announced it will not remove third-party cookies from Chrome and will not roll out a new standalone prompt either.
I have disabled the CI test job for now. It has been red for two weeks because of the flaky integration tests and people are merging around it. Until someone owns the suite, CI is effectively running
The new mapping with explicit nested fields accepts partial document updates. Incremental indexing is on in staging and the nightly full rebuild is no longer needed there.

Rolled incremental indexing back in production. Update storms during bulk imports pushed indexing lag past 40 minutes. Until the mapping is reworked again the index still cannot take incremental updat
Every deploy now ships with a reversible migration and a one-command rollback. Rollback was exercised in production twice this week; no manual database restore is needed any more.
Amazon RDS now supports customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Existing instances can be migrated with a snapshot restore.
Stripe multi-currency remains off on our account. Finance wants to keep a single settlement currency until the EU entity exists.
We will not shard Postgres by tenant. The Citus evaluation is closed; a single primary with read replicas covers projected load through 2027.
